newsitem.title: USA: Burger King eyes international growth.
newsitem.headline: Burger King eyes international growth.

text.p: Dennis Malamatinas, who was named chief executive of Grand Metropolitan Plc's Burger King Corp on Thursday, said his primary focus in his new position would be increasing the company's international market share.

Burger King's hamburger restaurants compete fiercely with those of McDonald's Corp in the United States, but Malamatinas noted that only about 20 percent of Burger King's sales come outside of North America.
"That's my primary job, my primary focus... We'd like to increase that," he said in a telephone interview.
He said the company was in a strong position.
"I think the company is in great shape, it is probably in the best shape it's been during its history," he said.

Burger King, the second-largest U.S. fast food chain, after McDonald's, has been gaining ground on its larger rival. Burger King's share of the U.S. quick-serve hamburger market rose to 19.2 percent last year from 18.2 percent a year earlier, while McDonald's slipped 0.2 percentage points to 42.1 percent.

Malamatinas said he viewed growth in Europe as the number one international opportunity, followed by the Asia/Pacific and Latin American markets. "Somehow, we'll have to learn how to move even faster, more aggressively," he said.

Malamatinas, 41, was most recently executive director and president of Grand Met's International Distillers and Vintners, Asia Pacific, the company's drinks business in Hong Kong. The company also announced Thursday that Paul Clayton, 38, who had been senior vice president of worldwide marketing for Burger King, was appointed to president of Burger King, North America, reporting to Malamatinas.
"We will be basically providing a dual focus on the business," Malamatinas said of himself and Clayton.
The new chief executive declined to make specific growth projections, or to discuss recent price cutting in the hamburger business initiated by McDonald's.
Clayton did offer a comment on some analysts' perception that fast-food chicken chains, notably Boston Chicken Inc, could be the fiercest competitor for U.S. fast-food dollars.

"They certainly compete for fast-food dollars," he said. But he noted Burger King's strong recent growth performance and said, "We continue to take market share away from our competitors... We're very confident about Burger King going forward."
Malamatinas said his initial priorities would be to get to know the members of his team and to get even better acquainted with the business.
